events.title: The attempt on the life of Pope John Paul II
events.shortBlurb: A gunman shot the Pope in St. Peter's Square on the anniversary of Fatima, and the Pope credited Our Lady with saving him…
body: On 13 May 1981, as John Paul II rode in an open car through St. Peter's Square at the start of his weekly general audience, the Turkish gunman Mehmet Ali Ağca fired four shots at close range, wounding the pope in the abdomen and hand; two bystanders were also hurt. Rushed to the Gemelli hospital, he survived five hours of surgery.

The date was the anniversary of the first apparition of Our Lady at Fatima in 1917, and the pope was certain her hand had spared him: 'one hand fired the shot,' he said, 'and another guided the bullet.' A year later he carried one of the bullets to Fatima, where it was set into the crown of the statue of Our Lady.

On 27 December 1983, in a cell of Rome's Rebibbia prison, the pope visited Ağca and forgave him face to face. Sentenced to life imprisonment, the gunman was pardoned by Italy in 2000 at John Paul's wish and sent home to Turkey.

sources.text: Vatican biography of Pope St. John Paul II (vatican.va)
